  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  March 10, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:07 p.m., on Monday, March 10, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Manager Analyst Alvarez, Public Information Specialist Rodriguez

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Lee

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  COMMENDATIONS: ALHAMBRA HIGH SCHOOL ACADEMIC DECATHLON TEAM –
  F2M25-3

  Mayor Lee, Councilmember Andrade-Stadler and the Alhambra City Council wished to
  congratulate and commend the Alhambra High School 2025 Academic Decathlon Team. For
  the second year in a row, the Team took first place out of 55 teams in the 43rd Annual Los
  Angeles County Academic Decathlon, after an outstanding performance in 10 subject areas
  including art, economics, essay, interview, language and literature, math, music, science,
  social science and speech. The Team scored a total of 47,430 points and took home a total of
  71 Medals, including 41 gold medals. The AHS Academic Decathletes were to be commended
  for their perseverance and dedication to scholastic excellence and the City of Alhambra
  celebrates their remarkable accomplishments. Mayor Lee presented commendations to the
  AHS 2025 Academic Decathlon Team members and coach. The Team members were as
  follows:
  KENNETH SAN
  KEVIN SAN
  OSCAR DIAZ
  CESAR GONZALEZ
  CLARISSA DIAZ
  MD HAMZA KHAN
  KAYLEE LU
  LYLA MEDINA
  ALEX WU
  1
3-10-25
   CARLOS CARRANZA
  Coach JOSE SANCHEZ

  Public Comment:
  1) F.D. spoke regarding the Academic Decathlon Team and went on to speak regarding First
  Amendment Rights.

  2) Kenneth SAN, the Academic Decathlon Team Captain listed the individual accomplishments
  of each team member and thanked Council for their support.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER spoke regarding the team’s victory and
  the support offered by the educators and administrators around them. Council offered their
  congratulations.

2.  COMMENDATIONS: ALHAMBRA HIGH SCHOOL BOYS SOCCER TEAM – ALHAMBRA
  UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT CUP CHAMPIONS – F2M25-3

  The Alhambra City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, wished to congratulate the
  Alhambra High School Soccer Team for their championship victory in the Alhambra Unified
  School District (AUSD) Cup. This marked the third time in a row Alhambra High School (AHS)
  has won the in-season Tournament between San Gabriel High School, Mark Keppel High
  School and AHS since its inception in 2023. AHS currently held the AUSD Cup record of 9
  wins, 2 losses, and 1 draw in 3 years. The Alhambra High School Boys Soccer Team was to
  be commended for demonstrating their ability to work together in a spirit of commitment,
  dedication and hard work and for winning their Third AUSD Cup! Mayor Lee presented
  commendations to the AHS Boys Soccer Team members and coaches. The Team members
  were as follows:

3.  PROCLAMATIONS – F2M25-3

  A.  The City Council ratified the action of Mayor Lee in proclaiming the month of March,
  2025 as WOMEN’S HISTORY MONTH in Alhambra. The proclamation would be
  mailed to the National Women’s History Alliance.

  Public Comment:
  1) Mistress Transgender Queen spoke regarding LGBT recognition and specifically
  transgender rights in the country, state, and City of Alhambra.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER addressed comments and stated that the City
  was supportive of various LGBT organizations and that the City was supportive of
  inclusion.

  2) F.D. spoke regarding Women’s History, the recognition of Women’s History Month,
  and Women’s rights.

  3) Lewis McCAMMON, via Zoom, spoke in favor of the proclamations and spoke
  regarding the history of Women’s voting rights in the United States and the 19th
  Amendment to the Constitution.

  B.  The City Council ratified the action of Mayor Lee in proclaiming March, 2025 as RED
  CROSS MONTH in Alhambra. The proclamation would be mailed to the San Gabriel
  and Pomona Valley Chapter of the American Red Cross.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M25-4
  1) Randy KAY, 723 W. Hellman Ave., spoke regarding the need for wildfire prevention and mitigation
  practices and went on to discuss various methods to reduce wildfire risks.

  2) Elizabeth Jacoby, 229 S. Meridian Ave., requested information as to whether City staff has received
  training in interacting with US. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

  3) Chandler Weber, 6501 Slyvan Rd., Citrus Heights, representing the U.S. Small Business
  Administration, spoke regarding the various services offered by their office. He discussed disaster
  assistance to businesses, non-profits, homeowners, and renters.

  4) Frederick Douglas recited transcripts from various legal cases and spoke regarding the importance
  of free speech and god.

  5) Mistress Transgender Queen spoke regarding DUI enforcement, alcohol and marijuana
  consumption, homelessness, and ICE enforcement.

  6) Gina Garcia, 819 N. Marguerita Ave., thanked Council and the City for the rapid installation of radar
  equipment in her neighborhood to limit speeding. She further requested greater traffic calming and
  safety measures throughout the City. She went on to discuss the natural disaster mitigation plan
  and her concerns regarding earthquakes in the City. She requested consideration of replacing
  infrastructure with flexible piping throughout the state.

PRESENTATIONS

4.  COMMUNITY  AGREEMENT  BETWEEN  WRENSMOOR  AND  ADJACENT
  NEIGHBORHOOD – F2M24-33
  3
3-10-25
   Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report. At their December 9, 2024
  meeting, the City Council heard feedback from residents adjacent to Wrensmoor about
  impacts to the neighborhood as a result of special events held at Wrensmoor Castle. The City
  Council directed Wrensmoor and the neighborhood to have meeting and discuss a path
  forward. Both parties have come to an agreement which stipulates conditions under which
  Wrensmoor would transition from its current business to one that will be compliant with the
  Alhambra Municipal Code and the short-term rental ordinance. Based upon Council’s prior
  direction to Wrensmoor to work with surrounding neighbors, Community Development staff
  intended to track Wrensmoor’s operations for consistency with the community agreement
  through the balance of 2025. Absent contrary direction from the Council, staff would enforce
  Chapter 5.92 at the Wrensmoor property beginning January 1, 2026, unless Wrensmoor
  should fail to adhere to the terms of the agreement with neighbors.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER reported on her meeting between the
  Community and the Operator of Wrensmoor. She briefly discussed the agreement made and
  expressed appreciation for Wrensmoor to work with the community to make an agreement.
  She supported the Community and their requests due to the location of Wrensmoor and close
  proximity to homes.

  Vice Mayor MALONEY and Mr. HO discussed the agreement, the community members
  involved, and a signed document which would be submitted to the City at a later date. Mr.
  MALONEY spoke in support of the agreement. He expressed hope that further agreements
  could be made with the community to better preserve the Wrensmoor property and prevent
  potential redevelopment of a historic property.

  Councilmember MAZA spoke in favor of the agreement, expressed similar concerns as his
  fellow Councilmembers, and expressed hope that Wrensmoor would improve relations with
  the community through 2025 and perhaps continue to operate. He requested a future
  discussion to update Council as to the progress.

  Councilmember WANG expressed appreciation for the work put into reaching this agreement
  and further discussed the plan for after 2025. Ms. Cordelia CULVER, representing Wrensmoor,
  discussed the community agreement and her responsibility to fulfill all commitments for 2025.
  She went on to discuss her hopes for the property as a feature of the community, her
  relationship with the neighboring community, and the company’s efforts to mitigate complaints.
  Ms. WANG reviewed the primary complaints and the plans to mitigate them. She suggested
  utilizing technology to mitigate the noise pollution in the neighborhood and Ms. CULVER
  discussed the sound system used for events. Ms. WANG supported an option of a trial period
  to try other improvements to see if the neighboring residents remain supportive of these efforts.

  Mayor LEE expressed sympathy for Wrensmoor but agreed with Ms. Andrade-Stadler that
  this was the wrong location for such a business. She commented on the responsibility of the
  property owner to discuss the proper uses of the property with Director Ho. Ms. LEE stated
  that she fully supported the residents and supported the agreement.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER expressed that the agreement was fair and gave Ms. Culver
  appropriate time to fulfil her commitments. She also stated that the main issue was parking
  which could not be entirely mitigated. She supported the agreement through 2025 only.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the community agreement between Wrensmoor
  and the neighborhood.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded: LEE
  Ayes:  WANG, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE,
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

 5.  COUNCIL CHAMBERS SAFETY – F2M25-7

  Police Chief KENNEDY delivered a presentation, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. At
  the January 27, 2025 Council meeting, Mayor Lee requested, and the City Council agreed to
  agendize, a presentation item regarding Council Chambers safety. Chief of Police Kennedy
  presented information regarding City Council meeting security overall, current safety
  procedures and recommended procedures for security during Council meetings. Additionally,
  the Chief provided a brief overview of some other Los Angeles County cities’ procedures. A
  copy of the presentation made by the Chief of Police is on file in the City Clerk’s Office.

  Public Comment:
  1) F.D. spoke regarding suppression of free speech, police violence, and made racist comments.
  He stated that any police search also be conducted on public employees. He related a case
  where he was banned from a Los Angeles City Council meeting.

  2) Mistress Transgender Queen suggested providing additional weaponry to Alhambra Police
  Department and requested assistance from additional agencies to help make Council feel
  safer. She went on to discuss the safety of Alhambra residents and the lack of response. She
  further related personal experiences and criticized Council.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor MALONEY thanked the Police Department for their presentation,
  expressed that he felt secure, and stated that he did not think there was a way to completely
  eliminate all potential threats in a public building. Councilmember MAZA echoed Mr. Maloney’s
  comments and stated that he felt there was no need to make any changes. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the responsibility of Council to receive comment from the
  public even when it was negative.

  Mayor LEE expressed that as an educator she felt safe until the events of the Columbine
  Colorado school shooting. She went on to discuss her concerns of future incidents, the
  perception of safety, and the need for caution and solutions. She further discussed school
  shootings and her experiences with active shooter drills. She requested obtaining price quotes
  for metal detectors at the front doors. She discussed a recent shooting of a Los Angeles pastor
  and the actions of an off-duty police officer.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed price quotes for metal
  detectors. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER requested that the information be provided to the Mayor.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 14)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 7, 9, 10, and 11, were
considered by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

6.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON
  ALMANSOR STREET – F2M24-52, C2M24-59, M2M25-22

  On September 23, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract to GRBCON Inc. for the Sewer
  Main Replacement Project on Almansor Street in the amount of $219,579. There were no
  change orders authorized to complete the project. However, there was a bid quantity
  adjustment made which decreased the total amount of the contract by $406, for a total project
  cost of $219,173. The project was completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and
  specifications. As such it was appropriate for the City Council to accept the project as complete

  Recorder’s Office.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

7.  RESOLUTION TO ADJUST THE CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION LIMIT PER THE
  REQUIREMENTS OF CHARTER SECTION 101C(C) – F2M23-36, R2M25-11

  Staff requested that the City Council adopt a Resolution to adjust the campaign contribution
  limit from $280 to $300. Section 101C(C) of Alhambra’s Charter states: “The City Council shall
  adjust the contribution limits established in this section in March of every odd numbered year
  to reflect any increase or decrease in the California Consumer Price Index since the last such
  adjustment of the contribution limit. Such adjustments shall be rounded to the nearest ten and
  no/100ths ($10.00) dollar amount.” The campaign contribution limit amount was adjusted to
  $280 by Resolution No. R2M23-16 on March 27, 2023. The timeframe utilized to measure the
  CPI change at that time was December, 2020 (when the initial campaign contribution limit
  amount was set at $250) through December, 2022. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor
  Statistics, the CPI change from December, 2022 through December, 2024 is 6.9%. Therefore,
  the current campaign contribution amount of $280, rounded to the nearest $10 would become
  $300.

  Discussion: Councilmember WANG discussed the Item, the past Measure V Campaign
  Finance Reform measures, and further explained the Resolution. She clarified that Measure
  V applied to all Council candidates. Councilmember MALONEY also provided clarification
  regarding the restrictions of Measure V as it applied to campaign contributions. Mayor LEE
  also commented on Measure V, her record of support for the Measure, and the benefits of
  campaign contribution limits.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-11 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council adjusting the campaign contribution limit per the requirements of
  Charter Section 101C(C)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  PARK NAMING AT FREMONT POCKET PARK, DOG PARK AND STORY PARK
  VACATED POOL SITE – F2M25-16, M2M25-24

  As part of the adopted 2024 Strategic Plan, staff is expanding greenspace throughout the
  community. Staff has been developing a “pocket park” located at Fremont and Hellman
  Avenue, the first-ever dog park, and expanding green space at the vacated Story Park pool.
  Staff has worked with the Parks and Recreation Commission to discuss “New Park Names”
  for the three new parks being developed throughout the City. At the February 2025 Parks and
  Recreation Commission meeting, staff presented several naming options per park to the
  Commission. The park names that the Parks and Recreation Commission is recommending
  are as follows: Little Midwick Park for the Pocket Park at Fremont and Hellman; Alhambra Pup
  Plaza for the Dog Park adjacent to the Golf Course; and, Serenity Circle for the park located
  at the site of the vacated Story Park pool adjacent to the Joslyn Center.

  Public Comment:  F.D. stated that he felt the money for this project could be better used
  in the development of veterans housing.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and City Manager BINNQUIST
  discussed the location of the Fremont Pocket Park in proximity to the Midwick Tract. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER requested that the naming of the Fremont Pocket Park be pulled from
  this agenda until more information could be provided regarding the Pocket Park’s location.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the new park names for the Dog Park to
  Alhambra Pup Plaza and the Story Park vacated pool site to Serenity Circle; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. Due to a question from
  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER regarding the location of the Fremont Pocket Park, no
  name was approved for this park. (M2M25-24)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  NIB: CITYWIDE BUS STOP IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT – F2M21-68, N2M25-29

  On March 14, 2022, staff awarded a contract to provide assessment and professional design
  services for the Citywide Bus Stop Improvements Project as well as preparation of plans,
  specifications and cost estimates for construction. The scope of work included, but was not
  limited to, identifying and designing for broken and off-grade sidewalk reconstruction, bus pad
  7
3-10-25
   installation, street furniture upgrades, ADA compliance, and 85 bus shelter upgrades or
  installations. Plans and specifications were prepared for this project. Staff reviewed the plans,
  which are in conformance with the City’s standards. Once approved, the specifications would
  be posted and advertised with the bid notice and bid instructions.

  Public Comment:
  1) F.D. related his experience filing an ADA Compliance request in 2012 with the City of Los
  Angeles and spoke against local government and specifically the City of Los Angeles.

  2) Mistress Transgender Queen spoke regarding safety on public transportation, the need for bus
  shelters with shade coverage, and the slow police response in the City.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER reported on other public transportation
  services in the City such as Senior Ride and the ACT Bus. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  requested an update as to federal funding for improvements. City Manager BINNQUIST stated
  that the City was confident that the total amount of funding would be available. She went on to
  discuss the project timeline and the scope of the project.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  Citywide Bus Stop Improvements Project, with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on April 13,
  2025; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

11.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A REVISED COMPREHENSIVE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING (MOU) WITH THE ALHAMBRA POLICE DISPATCHERS’
  ASSOCIATION (APDA) – F2M25-2, C2M21-51, R2M25-12, M2M25-25

  City staff and the Alhambra Police Dispatchers’ Association representatives reached
  agreement on the adoption of a new work schedule for dispatchers. The new “3/12.5” hour
  schedule for Police Department dispatchers is similar to that of Police Patrol personnel and
  would enable dispatchers to participate in patrol briefings and work more closely with Patrol
  personnel. This item aligned with the City Council’s Strategic Plan priority to “Enhance Public
  Safety.” Dispatchers are considered first responders and work closely with and provide support
  to the City’s public safety personnel on emergency response calls. There would be a cost
  saving associated with the adoption of a new dispatcher staffing schedule as it would no longer
  to necessary to schedule “overlap” shift coverage for dispatchers.

  Public Comment:  F.D. spoke against the item and against local government.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-12 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council approving a Revised Comprehensive Memorandum of
  Understanding between the City of Alhambra and the Alhambra Police Dispatchers’
  Association; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M25-25)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE

 12.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: LEASE OF SOLAR TRASH COMPACTORS – F2M17-38,
  C2M17-41, M2M25-26

  On June 26, 2017, the City entered into a contract with Big Belly Solar, LLC to lease eleven
  solar powered Big Belly + Smartbelly Double Stations with custom wraps and foot pedals
  though July 2022. The eleven units are located throughout the City. There have been two
  contract amendments since 2017. Amendment One to enable two additional units at Garfield
  Avenue through March 2025 and Amendment Two to renew the lease of the original eleven
  solar powered stations units through 2027. This Third Amendment would renew the lease of
  the two units at Garfield Avenue for a total cost of $12,803.28 through July 2027. The
  Amendment not only authorized expenditures for continued use of the units, but also changed
  the performance period so that the lease dates of all Big Belly stations align and expire on
  July 20, 2027.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Third Amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to the agreement (Contract No. C2M17-41)
  between the City of Alhambra and Big Belly Solar, LLC for continued lease of two solar trash
  compactors from March 20, 2025 through July 20, 2027 for an amount not to exceed
  $12,803.28; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M25-26)

 COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS) – F2M25-7

Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked staff for their work. She referred to public comment
made by Ms. Jacoby and requested staff contact the US. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
Department regarding areas where they may conduct searches as they would relate to Senate Bill 54,
the support for which was recently reaffirmed by Council. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER stressed the
importance of allowing all residents to feel safe when reporting a crime.

Vice Mayor MALONEY discussed the City’s partnership with the Clean Power Alliance and reported
on his membership on the Board for Clean Power Alliance stating that they were the largest provider
of renewable energy in the country. He requested a presentation given by a representative from the
Clean Power Alliance to provide additional information to Council and the public. Mr. MALONEY went
on to report on his membership in the API Caucus in the League of California Cities and provided
updates.

Councilmember WANG reported on the series of Sustainability Plan town hall meetings and reported
on the feedback she received from members of the public. She also reported on a Neighborhood
Watch meeting she was hosting at Granada Park on March 16th.

Mayor LEE made announcements regarding the upcoming Green Street Demonstration Project on
Main Street event and presentation and the public input portion for the Hazard Mitigation Plan.

Ms. LEE requested an agendized discussion of the Land Acknowledgment and Mission Statement
listed on the agendas of City Council meetings. She stated that the Land Acknowledgement lacked
sensitivity to the diversity of the community. She requested that the opening statement be more
inclusive and reflect the diversity of the community and its many ethnic groups. Ms. ANDRADE-
STADLER and Ms. LEE went on to discuss the language in the Land Acknowledgement. City Attorney
MONTES reminded Council to not fully discuss the proposed item, and to just acknowledge if they
support an agendized discussion. Ms. LEE clarified that she would like an Opening Statement which
would expand on the Land Acknowledgement and be more inclusive of the diversity in the community
and reflect the City’s Mission Statement. Mr. MALONEY did not support reopening discussion of the
Land Acknowledgment, but did support allowing the Mayor to read the Mission statement in full. Ms.
WANG and Mr. MONTES discussed the Mayor’s discretion to alter or not read the Land
Acknowledgement. Councilmember MAZA also did not support alteration to the Land
Acknowledgement, but agreed with Mr. Maloney’s suggestion to allow the Mayor to read the Mission
Statement at the start of the meeting. Ms. LEE and Mr. MONTES discussed the Mayor’s discretion to
provide an opening statement. Ms. LEE accepted that it was the Mayor’s discretion to read or alter the
